title: Motivated Monitors: The Importance of Institutional Investors' Portfolio Weights
abstract: We examine how the portfolio weight of a stock in an institutional investor's portfolio affects the investor's monitoring intensity and governance impact. Higher portfolio weights significantly increase active voting participation, direct intervention, and shareholder value creation during proxy fights.

title: Target Firm Advertising and Firm Value in Mergers and Acquisitions
abstract: This paper investigates strategic corporate advertising by target firms during takeover bids. We show that targeted advertising increases brand visibility, raises takeover premiums, reduces bid completion times, and enhances shareholder returns by resolving information asymmetry.

title: Frenemies: How Do Financial Firms Vote on Their Own Kind?
abstract: We analyze voting behavior when institutional asset managers vote on shareholder proposals at peer financial institutions. Financial firms exhibit strategic voting lenient toward industry peers unless market competition or regulatory pressure enforces strict governance.

title: Executive Compensation Structure and Takeover Vulnerability
abstract: We examine how equity-based executive compensation and severance packages (golden parachutes) influence target management incentives and negotiation outcomes during friendly vs. hostile acquisitions.

title: Institutional Investor Horizons and the Synergy Realization in Corporate Mergers
abstract: Long-term institutional ownership in acquiring firms promotes post-merger integration efficiency, operational synergies, and long-term stock outperformance following major corporate transactions.
